A restaurant-specific computer vision system for food and calorie logging can achieve state-of-the-art performance, outperforming previous computer vision methods as well as a commercial app.

(1) restaurant plates are often nutritionally and visually similar across multiple servings; (2) this observation provides a path to calorie estimation from a photograph; (3) our approach achieves better calorie estimation than existing computer vision and commercial methods; (4) our Menu-Match dataset provides a challenging testbed for future research.

(1) we introduce the Menu-Match dataset, which consists of 2,400 images of real restaurant meals and their corresponding calorie information, (2) we introduce a key insight, that restaurant plates are often nutritionally and visually similar, (3) we introduce a new computer vision approach for restaurant-specific food logging that leverages this insight and outperforms previous methods and a commercial food logging app, and (4) we make the Menu-Match database and source code publicly available.
